focus: Open-access availability of the biomedical literature (full text vs abstract only) and its consequences for text mining and machine reading
context: Hook: Curated knowledge bases such as OMIM are built by experts who read papers and record, entry by entry, what each paper showed; language models can now read those papers, and many system designs (long-context reading, extraction into graphs or tables, agents, draft-then-verify, prompt optimisation) have been proposed for turning documents into structured, cited text, but they were evaluated on different tasks, models, retrieval stacks and scoring, so their results cannot be compared.. Gap: There is no controlled evaluation in which the cited sources, the model, the mechanical guards and the scoring are held fixed and only the generation strategy varies, scored against curator-written per-paper text and structured fields. Scoped to what the log evaluates: one model family, 100 small OMIM phenotype entries (2-12 references) given the curators' own reference list, open-access text only; questions are (1) how much the strategy matters, (2) whether the strategy or what it could read limits agreement with curators, and (3) what a claim-level audit against the cited source can and cannot catch. No claim of generality across models, of clinical use, or of human validation.

section: Related Work: 2.1 Language models for literature curation in genetics and biology
focus: large language model rare disease phenotype profile generation compared with curated reports
context: Mission: Find work up to 2026-11 that uses language models to populate or assist curated biological knowledge bases (FlyBase/GO-style annotation, HPO annotation, ClinVar/variant evidence, gene-disease validity, rare-disease profiles), with emphasis on how each is evaluated: what reference, whether sources are fixed, whether curator-written text is used. Include the closest prior work named in notes.md (FlyAOC, GEN-KnowRD, WikiCrow, Groza et al. 2026) and phenotype concept-recognition baselines. Do not look for new systems to compare against; none were run.. Hypothesis: Prior work varies the retrieval, the model and the scoring together, scores against structured annotations or encyclopedia text rather than curators' per-paper prose, or tests what the model remembers rather than what it reads; none holds the cited papers fixed and varies only the generation strategy.

section: Related Work: 2.3 Memory, verification and contamination
context: Mission: Find work on generating from model memory and then verifying (chain-of-verification, self-verification against databases), and on detecting or measuring benchmark contamination (time-based splits, black-box tests), up to 2026-11. Look for evidence on whether verification after recall adds content or only removes/corrects it.. Hypothesis: Verify-after-recall methods are mostly evaluated on short-form or general-knowledge tasks where memory is strong; contamination studies rarely provide a control that measures what memory alone supplies for the same task and how this changes with when the knowledge was created.

section: Related Work: 2.4 Supervision by prompt optimisation
focus: automatic prompt optimization from natural language feedback
context: Mission: Find prompt-optimisation and reflective prompt-evolution methods (up to 2026-11) and their reported sample efficiency and evaluation settings, to position a small learned curation guide (two reflection rounds on 27 training entries).. Hypothesis: Prompt optimisation results are reported with substantial search budgets and on tasks with dense, cheap feedback; little is known about whether a guide learned from omissions and extras transfers to long-form knowledge-base writing with expensive scoring.

section: 3. Benchmark and Strategies - 3.3 Audit, scoring and statistics
focus: Efron (Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife)
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Completion as an outcome (idea.md 'Formal setup'; log Sec. 1.4): a strategy completes an entry when its draft exists and no per-paper call failed; compare only on entries every compared strategy completed; sensitivity analysis counts a missing draft as zero. Rationale: one-call strategies lose the entry, per-paper strategies lose a paper (idea.md 'Design rationale'). Audit: atomic claims attributed to cited papers; verdict v(c, d) in {supported, partly supported, unsupported, contradicted} with a quote that must occur verbatim, else downgraded; claim verdict is the best over R(c); one repair round. Report 'judged supported' and keep unsupported and contradicted separate (notes.md). Primary endpoint: coverage = (present + 1/2 partial) / facts judged over the fixed fact lists Phi(g); no fact went unjudged in any run (log Sec. 1.4). Explain why fixed lists: per-draft splitting adapts to the draft and changes denominators (idea.md; log Sec. 4.4). Secondary: HPO precision/recall/F1 exact, hierarchical (ancestors count) and semantic; allelic variant recall and precision matched on normalised protein or nucleotide change with a model judge for names that do not normalise, not validated against reference sequences; causal gene F1; inheritance agreement as coarse classes; predicting nothing where the gold set is non-empty scores zero (log Sec. 1.4). Statistics: paired differences from direct reading, bootstrap 95% interval over entries (10,000 resamples), median difference, exact sign test, Holm correction across secondary headline measures; primary endpoint not adjusted (log Sec. 1.4 and header). All verdicts and fact judgements are by the same model that wrote the drafts; no human validation.
